html:
The Regency of Algiers was a state in what is now northern Algeria, nominally part of the Ottoman Empire but in practice run by its own soldiers and sea captains from 1516 to 1830. The map shows it from 1715 to 1815.

It was founded by two corsair brothers, Oruç and Hayreddin Barbarossa, who took Algiers in 1516 and then placed it under the Ottoman sultan for protection against Spain. Algiers grew into a major base of the Barbary corsairs. They captured merchant ships and raided coasts as far as Ireland and Iceland, and the Barbary slave trade brought many thousands of Europeans to Algiers to be ransomed or worked.

From 1671 the ruler was a dey, elected by the Janissary garrison, and the link to Istanbul grew loose. European navies and the United States fought it in the Barbary Wars, and an Anglo-Dutch fleet bombarded Algiers in 1816. In 1830 France invaded, beginning French Algeria.
